turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale, I have a call at 4:40, so we have until then. My son found out he got a zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
I didn't come for the thanks. You entered a zero before anyone picked up a phone, and I'm still waiting to hear why.
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

A machine's guess, and you entered a zero on it. The company that sells that checker says in its own guide it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student," and your school's procedure 4.3 says the same thing. So is 94 percent all you have, Hale, or is there something else?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." Fourteen of these tools were tested in 2023 and the researchers called them "neither accurate nor reliable," and another study had detectors flagging 61 percent of essays by non-native English writers. I'm writing down that you called it reliable, Hale, so tell me what else you have before I go upstairs.
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Your own procedure says you speak to the student first and call the parent before any mark goes in, and you did neither. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
I hope you understand my position.

Your position is that a machine said 94 percent and you entered a zero without a phone call. I asked you a yes-or-no question and you didn't answer it, which I'm also writing down. Withdraw the zero, Hale, or show me something with a date on it.
